extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing examiner practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance from the MPEP on how examiners should prepare, sign, mail, and prioritize Office actions, when to limit action to specific issues, and the standards and procedures for petitions to make an application special (including accelerated examination and numerous special-status categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid secondary rejections when prior art discloses the 'heart' of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where there exists a sound rejection on the basis of prior art which discloses the “heart” of the invention (as distinguished from prior art which merely meets the terms of the claims), secondary rejections on minor technical grounds should ordinarily not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply restraint: if principal prior art defeats the invention's core, do not add minor technical rejections. Recognize limits of language; certain technical rejections (e.g., negative limitations, indefiniteness) should not be made where the examiner, recognizing the limitations of the English language, is not aware of an improved mode of definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit action on claim to a particular issue in specified situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some situations exist where examination appears best accomplished by limiting action on the claim to a particular issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations include: (A) application too informal for complete action (see MPEP §702.01); (B) undue multiplicity of claims where telephone election request unsuccessful (see MPEP §2173.05(n)); (C) misjoinder of inventions with no successful election request (see MPEP §§803, 806.02, 812.01); (D) disclosure directed to perpetual motion—in such cases cite best prior art and its pertinency without specifically applying it to the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections for res judicata/no prima facie/new matter/inoperativeness must be accompanied by other available grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection on the grounds of res judicata, no prima facie showing for reissue, new matter, or inoperativeness (not involving perpetual motion) should be accompanied by rejection on all other available grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asserting these substantial rejections, also state all other applicable rejections to fully inform applicant of the Office's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference instruction: See MPEP §714.23 regarding notifying of inaccuracies in amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Cross-reference entry — examiner should follow MPEP §714.23 when amendment inaccuracies are present.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Each pending claim must be mentioned in every letter
rubrics_metrics.description: In every letter, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude each action with a summary of all claims presented for examination. Claims retain original numerals throughout prosecution to make their history traceable. Maintain and keep the Index of Claims up to date per MPEP §719.04. Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 should be treated per MPEP §821–§821.03 and §809.02(c). See also MPEP §2363.03 for treatment in interference losing party application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft claims for pro se (inventor-filed) applications when patentable subject matter apparent
rubrics_metrics.description: When, during the examination of a pro se application it becomes apparent to the examiner that there is patentable subject matter disclosed in the application, the examiner should draft one or more claims for the applicant and indicate in his or her action that such claims would be allowed if incorporated in the application by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice expedites prosecution and serves individual inventors unfamiliar with proper preparation and prosecution. It is permissible in any appropriate case but expected to be applied where applicant appears unfamiliar with proper preparation/prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable except as to form — be constructive and suggest corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application discloses patentable subject matter but claims cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection; the action should be constructive and offer a definite suggestion for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner is satisfied that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and applicant intends to claim it, note unclaimed aspects that may be given favorable consideration if properly claimed. Suggest possible desirability of an interview to accelerate agreement on allowable claims. If a claim is otherwise allowable but dependent on a canceled or rejected claim, state it would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early allowance of clearly allowable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner is satisfied that the prior art has been fully developed and some of the claims are clearly allowable, the allowance of such claims should not be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs (e.g., 7.97 ‘Claims Allowed’) to indicate allowance. Do not withhold allowance of clearly allowable claims for procedural convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to indicate objection/allowable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, and 7.43.02 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter and to state specific conditions under which claims would be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include ¶7.43 to note dependency upon rejected base claim but allowability if rewritten; 7.43.01/7.43.02 specific to 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph rejections. Use form paragraph 7.97 for allowance. Follow examiner notes: use paragraphs only where appropriate (e.g., 7.43.01 only when independent claims were rejected solely under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number paragraphs consecutively in Office letters
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to number the paragraphs of the letter consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive numbering facilitates later identification and reference during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not question test/example results without reasonable basis; reject for insufficient disclosure if questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of tests and examples should not normally be questioned by the examiner unless there is reasonable basis for questioning the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner questions results, appropriate claims should be rejected as based on insufficient disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (In re Borkowski). Applicant must reply or provide actual test results or relevant arguments; take care not to introduce new matter. If operability/utility concerns exist, consider rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include examiner contact and telephone inquiry paragraph in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The full surname of the examiner who prepares the Office action will be typed at the end of the action and a telephone number should be provided for discussions or interview arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.100, 7.101 or 7.102. In 7.101/7.102, insert name, direct number, normal duty days/hours, supervisor contact if unreachable, group fax and receptionist numbers, and relevant schedule details (e.g., 5/4/9 schedule specifics). Ensure correct insertion of bracketed information per Examiner Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and initialing by assistant examiner — record preparer and date
rubrics_metrics.description: After the action is typed, the examiner who prepared the action reviews it for correctness; the surname or initials of the preparer and the date should appear below the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the preparer lacks signing authority, they should initial above the typed name or initials and forward to authorized signatory for signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing by primary or authorized examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Although only the original is signed, the word 'Examiner' and the name of the signer should appear on the original and copies. All letters and issues should be signed promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely signature by the authorized examiner and appropriate name placement on original and copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and recordation of original signed action
rubrics_metrics.description: The original, signed by the authorized examiner, is the copy placed in the file wrapper; the character of the action, its paper number and date of mailing are entered in black ink on the outside of the file wrapper under 'Contents'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate file wrapper entries reflecting the original signed document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing date stamped after signing
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing date should not be typed when the letter is written, but should be stamped or printed on all copies of the letter after it has been signed by the authorized signatory examiner and the copies are about to be mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pre-type mailing date; stamp/print at time of mailing to ensure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing of copies after original is initialed and signed
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the examiner’s action are mailed by the group after the original, initialed by the assistant examiner and signed by the authorized signatory examiner, has been placed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After copies are mailed the original is returned for placement in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling returned Office actions (undeliverable mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: If letters are returned because USPS could not deliver them, the examiner should use every reasonable means to ascertain the correct address and forward the letter again, stamping it 'remailed' with the date and redirecting if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period against the application begins with the date of remailing (Ex parte Gourtoff). If final delivery unsuccessful, place returned letter and envelope in file wrapper. If period from remailing elapses with no communication, forward case to Abandoned Files Repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination: priority by effective filing date with limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications are assigned and taken up for examination in the order in which they have been filed (effective U.S. filing date), except for applications advanced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.102 or other authorized exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each examiner gives priority to the application in their docket with the oldest effective U.S. filing date. Continuation-in-part docketing uses actual filing date; examiner may act using effective filing date if desired. If effective filing date status differs from records, notify technical support to amend records promptly. Examiners should prioritize reissue applications, reexamination, cases in litigation, special cases with set due dates, etc. Act promptly on cases clearly in condition for allowance or final rejection rather than letting them wait.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of special cases that are advanced out of turn
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of applications are advanced out of turn for examination (special cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) applications where inventions are of peculiar importance to public service and Commissioner orders immediate action (37 CFR 1.102); (B) applications made special by petition (see MPEP §708.02); (C) reissues particularly in stayed litigation (37 CFR 1.176); (D) applications remanded by appellate tribunal; (E) applications transferred and treated as special; (F) applications appearing to interfere with other applications or patents; (G) applications ready for allowance except formal matters; (H) applications in condition for final rejection; (I) applications pending >5 years (see MPEP §707.02); (J) reexamination proceedings (MPEP §2261). Special procedural priorities (e.g., examiner's answers) also take precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special — general regulatory basis and overview
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.102 provides that applications will not be advanced out of turn except as provided or upon order of the Commissioner or upon filing of requests/petitions under specified paragraphs (b)-(d). Certain petitions may be filed without fee (e.g., applicant's age/health or environmental/energy benefits), others require the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New applications ordinarily taken in order of effective filing date; exceptions made by petitions that meet stated conditions. If petition defective, applicant notified and given opportunity to perfect; if perfected in first renewed petition, granted; otherwise may be considered at Group Special Program Examiner discretion. Once granted, special status continues throughout prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for prospective manufacture — requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special on the ground of prospective manufacture upon filing a petition accompanied by the fee and a statement alleging possession of sufficient presently available capital (approximate amount) and facilities (nature), or that such will be made available if a patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prospective manufacturer is an individual, a corroborating statement from a responsible party (e.g., bank officer) is required to show available capital. Petition must state that the prospective manufacturer will not manufacture or increase manufacture unless certain patent will be granted; obligate to manufacture in the U.S. upon allowance; and state that a careful/thorough search of the prior art was made or that applicant has good knowledge of pertinent prior art. Applicant must provide one copy of each referenced prior art deemed most closely related if not already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for actual infringement — requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special because of actual infringement (not prospective infringement) upon payment of the petition fee and a statement alleging (A) infringing device/product/method actually on the market or in use; (B) a rigid comparison has been made and some claims are unquestionably infringed; (C) a careful and thorough prior art search was made or applicant has good knowledge of pertinent prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must provide one copy of each reference deemed most closely related if not already of record. Models or specimens of the infringing product should not be submitted unless requested. Further showing may be required depending on facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for applicant's health
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon petition by applicant accompanied by any evidence showing that the state of health of the applicant such that he might not be available to assist in prosecution (e.g., doctor's certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee required for such a petition (37 CFR 1.102(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for applicant's age
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon filing a petition including evidence showing that the applicant is 65 years of age or more (e.g., birth certificate or applicant's statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee required for such a petition (37 CFR 1.102(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for environmental quality inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord special status to patent applications that materially enhance the quality of the environment by contributing to restoration or maintenance of air, water, or soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should petition and include statements under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how the invention contributes to restoration/maintenance of these life-sustaining elements. No fee is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for energy-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord special status to inventions that materially contribute to discovery/development of energy resources or to efficient utilization/conservation of energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants petition with statements under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how the invention materially contributes to category (A) discovery/development (fossil fuels, nuclear, solar etc.) or (B) efficiency/conservation. No fee required (37 CFR 1.102(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for inventions relating to recombinant DNA safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord special status to patent applications relating to safety of research in recombinant DNA upon appropriate petition and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should be accompanied by statements under 37 CFR 1.102 by applicant/assignee/attorney/agent explaining the relationship of the invention to safety of recombinant DNA research; fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) must also be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites for accelerated (special) examination of new applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application (one not yet examined) may be granted special 'accelerated examination' status only if applicant complies with each of: (A) submits petition with fee; (B) presents all claims directed to a single invention or makes an election without traverse; (C) submits a statement that a pre-examination search was made listing field of search by class/subclass, publications, Chemical Abstracts, foreign patents, etc.; (D) submits one copy each of the references deemed most closely related if not already of record; (E) submits a detailed discussion of the references pointing out, with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c), how the claimed subject matter is patentable over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request does not meet prerequisites, applicant notified of defects and given one opportunity to perfect the petition in a renewed petition. If perfected, request granted; if not, further renewed petitions may be considered at Group Special Program Examiner discretion. Divisional applications to non-elected inventions must meet requirements on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for accelerated examination once special status granted
rubrics_metrics.description: The accelerated examining procedure involves: (A) examiner takes up application before other categories (except those clearly in condition for allowance) and gives a complete first action including all essential matters of merit; first action rejections set a 3-month shortened period for reply; (B) during 3-month reply period applicant encouraged to arrange interview and should provide proposed amendment at least one working day prior to interview (not part of file); (C) subsequent 'record' reply must be restricted to the rejections/objections/requirements made and must not broaden the search field; (D) examiner will, within 1 month of receipt of formal reply, take up the application for final disposition (either final action with 3-month period for reply or notice of allowance); (E) personal interviews after a final Office action not permitted unless requested by the examiner, but telephonic interviews allowed to correct minor matters. After allowance, these applications are given top priority for printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines are strict (3-month reply, 1-month final disposition). Keep amendments within scope to avoid new search. Use telephone for minor issues where appropriate. Once in program, there is no withdrawal from special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for superconductivity inventions — request without fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will, on request, accord special status to patent applications for inventions involving superconductivity materials (materials, manufacture, application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants desiring participation should request special status accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 that the invention involves superconductive materials. No fee required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for HIV/AIDS and cancer inventions — petition and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord special status to patent applications relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer. Applicants should file a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) requesting special status, accompanied by a statement explaining how the invention contributes to diagnosis, treatment, or prevention of HIV/AIDS or cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text also references that applicants should state small entity status or include statement establishing small entity status where applicable. Follow petition/fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for counter-terrorism inventions — petition and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord special status to patent applications relating to counter-terrorism inventions. Applicants should file a petition with the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) and a statement explaining how the invention contributes to countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International terrorism (18 U.S.C. 2331) defined; example technologies include explosive detection/identification, aircraft sensors/security systems, vehicular barricades/disabling systems. Petition should explain contribution; pay petition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for biotechnology applications filed by small entities — requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are small entities may request special status for biotechnology applications by filing a petition with the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) and must: (B) state that the subject of the patent application is a major asset of the small entity; and (C) state that development of the technology will be significantly impaired if examination of the patent application is delayed, including explanation of the basis for the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow fee/statement requirements carefully; demonstrate the major asset status and the impairment to development from delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of petition to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special should be in writing and identify the application by application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure petitions are written and include clear application identification to be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of petitions to make special — continued special status
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications which have been made special will be advanced out of turn for examination and will continue to be treated as special throughout the entire prosecution in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once special status is granted, it continues for the complete prosecution including appeal if any; divisions do not automatically inherit special status and must meet requirements themselves.
